Abyssal Engine

A lightweight, modular WebGPU game engine and editor built to create the worlds of Keyless Abyss.

Abyssal Engine exists to build real games, beginning with Morninghollow. The manual is the official learning path for developers, designers, and AI assistants before they touch code.

Open Abyssal Editor Learn the Engine AI Reading Order

Current Status

This hosted build is an evolving editor and engine preview. It demonstrates project-based authoring, WebGPU rendering, asset browsing, and Wings Assembler workflows.

WebGPU-first TypeScript Projects Wings Assembler Active development

Build games, not demos

Abyssal is shaped by Morninghollow and the needs of real game production. Features are added when they support a working content or gameplay path.

Project-owned content

Projects provide a disk home for Fragments, Materials, and future scenes or recipes. The editor is moving toward durable, native content assets.

Modular assembly

Meshes, Materials, Fragments, Constructs, and Components each have distinct responsibilities so content can grow without becoming one tangled object.

Documentation Notice

Abyssal Engine is under active development. This public manual describes the current hosted build and may evolve alongside the editor.

Learning Center

  • Engine Overview explains the public architecture.
  • Design Principles explains the rules behind engine decisions.
  • Controls lists verified editor inputs.
  • Features separates available, experimental, and planned systems.

Known Limitations

  • Best supported in a desktop Chromium browser with WebGPU.
  • Project folders require browser File System Access permission.
  • Scene persistence, texture assets, and production export workflows are not complete yet.
  • Some gameplay and stress systems remain diagnostic or experimental.
